prior_review_findings_addressed.pr5958_p2_registry_jwt_issuer_audience_f: This delivery: independently reproduced the reviewer's exact repro (`docker compose --env-file /dev/null config --format json` with only PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_ISSUER/AUDIENCE set and CAPITAL_JWT_*/PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_* issuer/audience unset). docker-compose.yml's PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_ISSUER/AUDIENCE (previously ${PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_ISSUER:-${CAPITAL_JWT_ISSUER:-pantheon-dev-control-plane}}, no PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_ISSUER fallback level) resolved to the literal default while operator-bff's own CAPITAL_JWT_ISSUER (which has that fallback level) resolved to the configured dev value -- because docker compose interpolation resolves every service's ${VAR:-...} independently against the top-level shell/.env environment, never against another service's own already-resolved container value. Fixed by adding the same PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_ISSUER/AUDIENCE fallback level operator-bff's own line already has (governance's equivalent chain already had this level and needed no change). Added a literal-string regression test (updated to match) plus a new behavioral regression test that runs the reviewer's exact `docker compose config` repro and asserts operator-bff/registry/governance all resolve identically for a non-default dev value.
prior_review_findings_addressed.pr5958_p1_ac5_hosted_reproduction_stoppe: This delivery: the prior delivery's evidence stopped at OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_INVOCATION_FAILED and speculated the remaining gap needed live third-party LLM provider credentials. That diagnosis was wrong: `cron.list`/`cron.add` are pure Gateway RPCs (job-scheduler admin calls) that never invoke a model at all. The actual remaining gap was OpenClaw's own one-time device-pairing/scope-approval flow (docs/runbooks/openclaw-adapter-device-pairing.md, scripts/openclaw-approve-adapter-cron-scope.sh -- both pre-existing, unmodified) plus two further, independently reproduced docker-compose.yml credential/tenant wiring gaps below the OpenClaw layer that the prior reproduction never reached. This delivery started the real openclaw-gateway container (COMPOSE_PROFILES=...,openclaw; no live LLM credentials configured or required), ran the adapter's device-pairing and cron-write-scope-upgrade dance exactly as the runbook documents, found and fixed the two further docker-compose.yml gaps below, and re-ran the real unmodified bootstrap to an authoritative persona state=paper_running end to end -- see verification.hosted_reproduction.

implementation.registry_jwt_issuer_audience_fallback_ch: docker compose interpolation resolves every service's ${VAR:-...} independently against the top-level shell/.env environment at parse time -- it does not read another service's own already-resolved container value. operator-bff's CAPITAL_JWT_ISSUER line (${CAPITAL_JWT_ISSUER:-${PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_ISSUER:-pantheon-dev-control-plane}}) and registry's PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_ISSUER line previously only chained through ${CAPITAL_JWT_ISSUER:-pantheon-dev-control-plane} (no PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_ISSUER fallback level of its own), so whenever the deploy environment exported PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_ISSUER/AUDIENCE but not CAPITAL_JWT_ISSUER/AUDIENCE itself (the dev-paper-principal-issuer profile's actual export contract, and scripts/issue_dev_paper_principals.py's own output), operator-bff correctly fell through to the configured dev value while registry's shorter chain fell straight to the unrelated literal default -- so registry's strict-mode JWT verification rejected every token operator-bff signed. Fixed by adding the missing PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_ISSUER/AUDIENCE fallback level to registry's chain, matching operator-bff's own line exactly (governance's chain already had this level, confirmed unchanged and correct by inspection and by the behavioral regression test).
implementation.deployment_tenant_id_hardcoded_default: runtime-manager's and deployment-outbox-consumer's PANTHEON_DEPLOYMENT_TENANT_ID both hardcoded the literal default 'default' (${PANTHEON_DEPLOYMENT_TENANT_ID:-default}), unlike every other tenant-scoped service in docker-compose.yml, which chains through ${PANTHEON_TENANT_ID:-${PANTHEON_BFF_TENANT_ID:-default}}. A real dev-paper bootstrap run authenticates as the dev-login operator, whose default allowed tenant is 'tenant-dev' (PANTHEON_BFF_DEV_LOGIN_OPERATOR_A_ALLOWED_TENANTS's first entry, and the same 'tenant-dev' default PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_TENANT_ID uses for the dev-paper-principal-issuer), so every persona/plan/saga this delivery's reproduction created lived under tenant 'tenant-dev'. deployment-outbox-consumer authenticates its own outbox-claim calls to the deployment service with X-Tenant-Id set from PANTHEON_DEPLOYMENT_TENANT_ID; with that hardcoded to 'default' it never matched any queued 'tenant-dev' event, so it silently claimed zero events on every poll tick forever (confirmed via its own health file: total_consumed stayed 0 across the entire run) -- no error surfaced anywhere, because the consumer's own tenant scoping 'worked' correctly for its own (wrong) tenant. The deployment saga (deployment-saga-<plan-id>) was correctly created (event #1, runtime.binding.requested) but never advanced, because nothing ever consumed it; the top-level persona-provisioning coordinator's own readback loop eventually timed out (provisioning_timeout) and triggered saga compensation/abort as designed -- a correct fail-closed response to a real, silent upstream stall, not a bug in the coordinator itself. Fixed by adding the same ${PANTHEON_TENANT_ID:-${PANTHEON_BFF_TENANT_ID:-...}} chain convention plus a PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_TENANT_ID fallback level (the specific var the dev-paper flow's tenant actually comes from) before the literal default, to both runtime-manager and deployment-outbox-consumer. This was found by advancing the hosted reproduction past the OpenClaw device-pairing gap (below) into the actual RuntimeBinding-creation path -- no prior delivery under this task had ever reached this step.
implementation.openclaw_device_pairing_not_an_llm_crede: The prior delivery's evidence stopped at 'openclaw gateway call cron.list exited 1: OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_INVOCATION_FAILED' and concluded the remaining gap required live third-party LLM provider credentials and outbound network egress. Independently verifying this: cron.list/cron.add/config.schema are pure OpenClaw Gateway RPCs (job-scheduler and config admin calls dispatched over the gateway's own WebSocket JSON-RPC transport) that never invoke a model provider at all -- confirmed by starting the real openclaw-gateway container with the compose file's existing `--allow-unconfigured` gateway command and no Claude/Gemini CLI login configured, then calling `openclaw gateway call cron.list` from the adapter container, which failed instead with `pairing required: device is not approved yet` (later `scope upgrade pending approval` for the write-scoped cron.add), exactly the symptom docs/runbooks/openclaw-adapter-device-pairing.md already documents and scripts/openclaw-approve-adapter-cron-scope.sh already automates. Running that pre-existing, unmodified runbook procedure (device pairing for operator.read/operator.write, then the cron-write operator.admin scope upgrade) let `openclaw gateway call cron.list` succeed cleanly with zero LLM provider credentials configured anywhere in the stack. This closes the prior delivery's speculative external-dependency conclusion: schedule_registration's cron.add call needs OpenClaw device pairing (a one-time, scriptable, credential-free gateway-side approval), not a live LLM provider.

hosted_reproduction.summary: Ran the real, unmodified scripts/bootstrap_dev_paper_baseline.py exactly as the real dev deploy invokes it (`docker exec <operator-bff-container> python /workspace/scripts/bootstrap_dev_paper_baseline.py --timeout-seconds 420 --poll-seconds 5`, per scripts/run_dev_paper_baseline_with_diagnostics.sh) against a full local docker compose deployment of this exact docker-compose.yml, including the real openclaw-gateway and openclaw-gateway-adapter services (COMPOSE_PROFILES=dev-paper-principals,openclaw). Isolated project (dpsp-repro2), unique 45xxx-50xxx ports, DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 classic builder (this session's Docker data dir constraint, not a product concern), built and started from a completely fresh set of named volumes/containers on a host that had never run any Pantheon service before (zero data_source_instances, zero prior personas, zero prior capital pools, zero prior OpenClaw device pairings -- satisfying AC1 and the 'never-provisioned first-run' half of AC5 literally). No live LLM provider credentials (Claude/Gemini CLI login) were configured anywhere in the stack for this reproduction. Reached a fully successful, authoritative persona state=paper_running end to end, then independently confirmed durability via an idempotent-replay bootstrap invocation and direct reads of the coordinator's own persisted receipts.
steps: docker compose -p dpsp-repro2 up -d --build (DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0) -> full ~50-service dependency graph including openclaw-gateway and openclaw-gateway-adapter built and started healthy.
GET connectors/snapshot checks on the fresh source-ingest container confirmed a genuinely never-provisioned host, as in the prior delivery's reproduction.

OpenClaw device pairing: `openclaw gateway call cron.list` from the adapter failed with 'pairing required: device is not approved yet'; `openclaw devices list --json` on the gateway showed the pending operator.read request; `openclaw devices approve <requestId>` approved it; cron.list then succeeded cleanly. Ran scripts/openclaw-approve-adapter-cron-scope.sh (unmodified, pointed at the reproduction's container names via its documented OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_CONTAINER/OPENCLAW_ADAPTER_CONTAINER env vars) to grant the operator.admin scope cron.add needs; it found the pending scope-upgrade request, approved it, and verified the adapter device now holds operator.admin/operator.read/operator.write. No LLM provider credential was configured or required for any of this.

Iteration 1 (docker exec bootstrap, default idempotency key): failed at baseline_approval_proposed with a persisted 'Scoped Persona Governance principal is required' error -- the dev-paper-provisioner grant's *_FILE env vars (PANTHEON_PERSONA_GOVERNANCE_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE, GOVERNANCE_DEV_PAPER_APPROVAL_ENABLED/GRANT_FILE) were unset by design (same class of deliberate-no-default activation gap the prior delivery documented); set them to the dev-paper-principal-issuer's already-mounted token files and re-ran.

Iteration 2: failed at baseline_approval_reviewed with governance returning 'HTTP Error 503: Registry candidate read unavailable' -- governance's own configured_paper_registry_reader needs GOVERNANCE_REGISTRY_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE to read the candidate registry entry back for verify_paper_candidate_for_decision; that var was unset by design (same class of gap). Pointed it at governance's own mounted token file and re-ran.

Iteration 3 (fresh idempotency key + persona name, since the first two personas were already terminally failed/compensated under their names): schedule_registration succeeded (cron.add, using the OpenClaw device pairing above) and the coordinator advanced to current_step=schedule_registered with no error -- past every point any prior delivery under this task had ever reached. The bootstrap process then ran for the full ~600s server-side provisioning timeout and the coordinator recorded a terminal provisioning_timeout, triggering deployment saga compensation.

Diagnosed the timeout: the deployment saga (deployment-saga-<plan-id>) was correctly created with event #1 (runtime.binding.requested) but deployment-outbox-consumer's own health file showed total_consumed=0 across its entire run -- it never claimed that event. Traced this to deployment-outbox-consumer authenticating its outbox-claim calls with X-Tenant-Id from PANTHEON_DEPLOYMENT_TENANT_ID, hardcoded to the literal 'default', while the saga (and every persona/plan under this bootstrap run) lives under tenant 'tenant-dev'. Fixed docker-compose.yml (see implementation.deployment_tenant_id_hardcoded_default) and re-ran with a fresh idempotency key.

Iteration 4: failed at authoritative_readback in ~12s (much faster -- confirming the consumer now claims the event immediately) with a persisted saga failure_reason 'transient dispatch failure: Registry scoped read principal required' -- runtime-manager's own deploy_authority module needs RUNTIME_MANAGER_REGISTRY_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE to read the registry candidate before creating the RuntimeBinding; that var was unset by design (same class of deliberate-no-default activation gap, distinct from the deployment-outbox-consumer's own aliased RUNTIME_MANAGER_REGISTRY_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE which was already correctly wired to deployment's mounted file). Pointed runtime-manager's own copy at its own mounted token file (dev-paper-runtime-tokens volume, already populated by the dev-paper-principal-issuer) and re-ran with a fresh idempotency key and persona name.

Iteration 5 (final): `{"attempts": 2, "capital_mode": "paper", "deployment_plan_id": "plan-persona-paper-6cb1cb4e6a96aa60e7fb", "live_capital_side_effects": false, "persona_id": "persona-e9a58ffe7c44604a3df2", "provisioning_state": "succeeded", "provisioning_step": "authoritative_readback_complete", "runtime_binding_id": "rb-c565de7ceb0e4be4b6247f44cad075cb", "runtime_id": "rt-7def8498", "state": "paper_running", "status": "ok"}` -- full success, authoritative paper_running, from a host with zero pre-existing data source instances, zero pre-existing personas, and zero pre-existing OpenClaw device pairings.

Durability/readback confirmation: re-ran the identical bootstrap invocation (same idempotency key and persona name) a second time; it replayed the terminal success idempotently in {"attempts": 1, ...} with the identical persisted state=paper_running, runtime_binding_id, and runtime_id, proving the success is a durable persisted receipt, not a transient in-flight report.

Independent persisted-receipt verification (bypassing bootstrap's own stdout summary entirely): `docker exec <postgres> psql -c "select persona_id, state, current_step, updated_at from bff.persona_provisioning ..."` showed state=succeeded, current_step=authoritative_readback_complete for the final persona; `docker exec <runtime-manager> python -c '...GET /api/runtime-bindings...'` returned the authoritative RuntimeBinding (binding_id=rb-c565de7ceb0e4be4b6247f44cad075cb) with its full authoritative_loader_attestation, including the exact governance approval_decision_id, its sha256, and the canonical deployment authority chain.

Cleanup: `docker compose -p dpsp-repro2 down -v` (all containers, the dedicated network, and every named volume including every token volume removed); session-built dpsp-repro2-* images removed via `docker rmi -f`. No dpsp-repro2 containers, networks, volumes, or images remain.
hosted_reproduction.note: Every gap found and fixed in this delivery (the P2 issuer/audience chain, and the newly discovered tenant-id chain) reproduced identically against the real, unmodified owner services this docker-compose.yml already defines -- none were artifacts of a mock or a simplified stand-in, and the terminal success state was independently confirmed via the coordinator's own persisted PostgreSQL receipt and runtime-manager's own authoritative RuntimeBinding read, not just bootstrap's stdout.

review_decision.note: Independently verify: (1) the reviewer's own P2 repro command now resolves registry identically to operator-bff; (2) the new PANTHEON_DEPLOYMENT_TENANT_ID chain fix is individually necessary (revert it locally, re-run a fresh dpsp-style reproduction through the deployment-dispatch step, and confirm deployment-outbox-consumer's total_consumed stays 0 and the saga stalls at runtime.binding.requested exactly as this evidence recorded); (3) the hosted_reproduction's claim of reaching authoritative state=paper_running against the complete, unmodified stack with zero LLM provider credentials configured -- in particular that OpenClaw device pairing/cron-scope approval is genuinely credential-free and not a disguised LLM call; (4) whether AC5 is now fully satisfied by this evidence, given the prior delivery's OpenClaw-gateway external-dependency conclusion is shown here to have been a misdiagnosis rather than a genuine remaining blocker.
